Native iOS music injection

Say goodbye to iTunes sync.

ByeTunes lets you add songs, albums, playlists, artwork, lyrics, and metadata directly to your iPhone media library — cleanly, quickly, and without the old sync ritual.

Download IPAView GitHub
Features

Built for people who want their music library back.

Native library

Direct Injection

Add music straight into the native iOS media library without the usual sync routine.

One-tap albums

Album Downloads

Grab full albums or choose individual tracks before sending them to your device.

Live queue

Queue Control

Keep an eye on every download with a clear queue, live state, and progress feedback.

Feels built in

Apple Music Ready

Injected tracks appear in the familiar iOS player with artwork, lyrics, and lock-screen controls.

Clean library

Metadata Editing

Tidy titles, artists, artwork, explicit tags, and playlist data before injecting.

Flexible files

Lossless Friendly

Designed for common music formats including MP3, M4A, WAV, and FLAC workflows.

In the app

Actual screens, not mock UI.

The product page shows the app as it really is: music queues, album selection, progress state, lock-screen playback, lyrics, and the on-device library.

Control panel

Build a queue, then inject it cleanly.

The main screen keeps music, playlists, and device status in one place.

Albums

Fast selection for full releases, with a clear count before download.

Progress

Follow every item in the queue.

A compact queue view shows what is active, what is waiting, and what comes next.

Lock-screen playback

Lyrics view

On-device library

Setup

Pair once. Use it every day.

The computer is only needed for the initial pairing certificate. After that, the app is designed around fast on-device music management.

1
Install LocalDevVPN and connect your device.
Usually done once, then kept out of the way.
2
Generate the pairing file once from your computer.
Usually done once, then kept out of the way.
3
Import the certificate into ByeTunes.
Usually done once, then kept out of the way.
4
Add songs, inject, and open them in Apple Music.
Usually done once, then kept out of the way.

Start building your music library.

Open-source, native-feeling, and designed for people who want direct control over their iPhone music.
